question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(120,0.41),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X<48).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3446\,$ | $\,0.3409\,$ | $\,0.3372\,$ |
| $\,-0.3\,$ | $\,0.3821\,$ | $\,0.3783\,$ | $\,0.3745\,$ |
| $\,-0.2\,$ | $\,0.4207\,$ | $\,0.4168\,$ | $\,0.4129\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=120$ and $p=0.41.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =120\cdot 0.41 \\  & =49.2 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =120\cdot (1-0.41) \\  & =70.8 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(120)(0.41)=49.2
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(120)(0.41)(1-0.41)=29.028.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(49.2,29.028).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(X<48).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X<48)=P(X\le 47)≈P(Y\le 47.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 47.5) & =P(Z\le \frac{47.5-49.2}{\sqrt{29.028}}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le -0.32) \\  & =Φ(-0.32) \\  & =0.3745\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X<48)≈0.375.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.3762.$
